title: Derived internal Hom into a complete object on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O$ be an ideal subsheaf. Use the unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived internal Hom $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and restriction to slice ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Call $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ locally derived $\mathcal I$-complete if for every object $U$ and every $f\in\mathcal I(U)$ one has $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],N|_U)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]; here $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-section-localization]. For every $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and every locally derived $\mathcal I$-complete $N$, the object $H(K,N)$ is locally derived $\mathcal I$-complete. No boundedness, finite-generation, finite-type-ideal, or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 099A, lemma-derived-complete-internal-hom; local completeness is Definition 0999.

proof.text: Fix an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and a section $f\in\mathcal I(U)$. Restriction of internal Hom to the slice identifies $H(K,N)|_U$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(K|_U,N|_U)$, using the localized ringed site and the exact slice restriction.

The tensor--internal-Hom adjunction on the slice gives a canonical isomorphism
$$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(K|_U,N|_U))\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f]\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_U}K|_U,N|_U).$$
This is the currying identity for derived internal Hom, with the localization supplied by the section-localization definition.

Put $S=\mathcal O_U[1/f]$. Derived extension of scalars along $\mathcal O_U\to S$ gives $K|_U\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_U}S\in D(S)$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Its underlying $\mathcal O_U$-object identifies with $S\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_U}K|_U$: on a K-flat representative $P$ the tensor interchange is $p\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes p$, with no sign since $S$ is in degree zero. Since $N$ is locally derived $\mathcal I$-complete, its localization Hom vanishes: $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],N|_U)=0$. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-localization-rhom-orthogonality] on the slice to conclude
$$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f]\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_U}K|_U,N|_U)=0.$$

source.place: Tag 099A, lemma-derived-complete-internal-hom, proof; Tag 0997, lemma-hom-from-Af; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change (identity underlying topos, coefficient map O_U to S)

proof.text: Combining the slice restriction from Step 1, the currying isomorphism of Step 2, and the vanishing of Step 3 gives $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],H(K,N)|_U)=0$. Since this holds for every $U$ and every $f\in\mathcal I(U)$, the defining criterion says that $H(K,N)$ is locally derived $\mathcal I$-complete.
